name: U.S. Outpatient Influenza-like Illness Surveillance Network
reports: The weekly percentage of outpatient visits meeting the influenza-like illness definition, reported by age group.
interpretation: Use it to follow how much outpatient care is for flu-like illness. Other respiratory viruses can cause the same symptoms, so this is not a count of confirmed influenza.

name: National Syndromic Surveillance Program
reports: The percentage of emergency-department visits with an influenza discharge diagnosis, overall and by age group.
interpretation: Use it to follow how much emergency care involves a flu diagnosis. Testing and coding practices affect the signal; a diagnosis does not always mean a positive test.

name: Influenza Hospitalization Surveillance Network
reports: Population-based weekly rates and detailed characteristics of laboratory-confirmed influenza hospitalizations in selected catchment areas.
interpretation: Use it to compare hospitalization rates across ages and seasons and identify who is most affected. Rates describe monitored communities, not every U.S. hospital.

name: National Healthcare Safety Network Hospital Respiratory Data Module
reports: Weekly facility-level counts of new laboratory-confirmed influenza admissions, current hospitalizations, ICU occupancy, and bed capacity.
interpretation: Use it to track admissions and pressure on hospital and ICU capacity. These are hospital totals, not detailed records of individual patients.

name: U.S. Influenza Collaborating Laboratories System
reports: Weekly influenza tests and positive results. Public-health laboratory reports include virus types, subtypes or lineages, and patient ages when available.
interpretation: Use clinical-lab positivity to follow flu activity and public-health results to identify circulating viruses. Public-health samples often arrive already positive, so their positivity is not a community infection rate.

name: National Respiratory and Enteric Virus Surveillance System
reports: Weekly test totals and positive results for influenza and other respiratory and enteric viruses, from hospital, commercial, and public-health laboratories.
interpretation: Use clinical-lab positivity to follow when and where flu is circulating. It describes tested specimens, not the percentage of all people infected.

name: National Center for Health Statistics Mortality Surveillance
reports: Weekly death-certificate measures for deaths coded with influenza, pneumonia, and/or COVID-19.
interpretation: Use influenza-coded deaths to follow flu's fatal impact over the season. Recent weeks are incomplete, and death certificates miss some deaths caused by flu.

name: Influenza-Associated Pediatric Mortality Surveillance System
reports: Individual laboratory-confirmed influenza-associated deaths among people younger than 18 years, with demographic and clinical details.
interpretation: Use it to track reported flu deaths in children and identify their clinical patterns. Recent counts can increase as additional reports arrive.
